The Terms of Service describe the "MindWell Sleep Study". Here's a plain-language summary:

The study looks at how a sleep-tracking app affects people with insomnia.

* To participate, you'll wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks, and every week, you'll fill out a survey.
* The Terms of Service say this is a "minimal risk" study, with the only possible discomfort being skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* Your data will be used in the study. Some data can be shared with other universities (de-identified data), but your personally identifiable data will only be shared within the research team.
* You can stop participating at any time without any consequences or penalties.
* Once you complete the study, you'll receive $75.

One thing to keep in mind: The terms don't fully explain what happens to your data after 8 weeks. They do say that identifiable data won't be shared outside the research team, but it might be shared with academics. There's no information about what specific actions will be taken with your data.

The Terms of Service assign you to contact the IRB (Institutional Review Board) at irb@example.edu with questions or concerns.

Note that there's no prior version to compare with, so there are no changes mentioned.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

- Risk is minimal; mainly possible skin irritation.
- De-identified data may be shared with collaborators; identifiable data is kept within the research team.
- Withdrawal is allowed at any time without penalty.
- Compensation is $75 on completion.

**Service Name:** The Google Terms of Service, which govern user relationships with Google and apply to various Google products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with Google and cover the products and services listed on the official Google terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Google (e.g., photos, posts), Google may use it to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** These terms don't explain data collection and processing directly, so for details, refer to Google's separate **Privacy Policy**, which describes categories of personal data collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The updated terms continue to require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with class-action waivers (this means you can't join a group lawsuit). You'll have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, subject to conditions outlined in the live document.

**Provisions that may be harmful to users:**

* **Data usage and AI training:** This may concern users if they're not aware of or don't agree how their content contributes to Google's AI/ML systems.
* **Dispute resolution:** The requirement for **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** and **class-action waivers** may leave users without the option for joining class-action lawsuits or court-based dispute resolution.
* **Termination**: Although users are alerted to termination conditions in the live document, a lack of transparency might make this difficult to discover promptly.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GOOGLE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Google and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: Added language about generative AI features (e.g. content used to improve Google's AI services), clarified that abuse and reverse-engineering of AI models are prohibited, and updated the disputes/arbitration and liability sections. Comparison page provided by Google: policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105-20240522.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Google to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en-US . The previous version is available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US .

**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement

**Summary:** The Microsoft Services Agreement is a contract between you and Microsoft that outlines the terms and conditions for using Microsoft's products and services. Think of it like a set of rules that govern the relationship between you (the user) and Microsoft.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on Microsoft's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Microsoft, they can use it to improve their services, train AI and ML systems, and more, but only according to your settings and the law.
* **Privacy:** Microsoft collects personal data and processes it according to their Privacy Policy. You can find the policy by looking at the relevant Microsoft service you're using.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users must resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which means you can't go to court. However, there's a 30-day window to opt out of this for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, you can contact Microsoft through the published legal contact information on their website.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Arbitration:** Mandatory arbitration might seem intimidating, especially if you're not familiar with the process. However, it's worth noting that there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, and some services (like Steam) have chosen not to include arbitration.
* **Personal Data:** Microsoft collects personal data, and you should review their Privacy Policy to understand how it's used and processed.
* **Auto-Renewal:** Some trial offers may automatically renew, so be sure to review the terms if you're considering signing up for a trial.

Overall, these Terms of Service provide a clear outline of the relationship between you and Microsoft. By understanding the key provisions and potential concerns, you can make informed decisions about how you use Microsoft's products and services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

**Summary of Microsoft Services Agreement (2023 → 2024)**

**Service Name:** This document governs the relationship between you and Microsoft for using their various products and services, including but not limited to Xbox.

**Key Provisions:**

* Microsoft uses your submissions to improve their products and train their AI/ML systems (Content and License, clause 3).
* Your personal data is governed by Microsoft's Privacy Policy, which outlines what they collect and how it's processed (Privacy, clause 4).
* Disputes are resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with some exceptions (Dispute Resolution, clause 5).
* Either party can terminate the agreement if they choose to (Termination, clause 6).

**Harmful or Concerning Clauses:**

* Dispute Resolution (clause 5): Most users are required to participate in binding arbitration, which can limit your ability to take action in a court of law. However, Steam users are exempt from this.
* Termination (clause 6): Both parties can terminate the agreement without warning, which may lead to immediate loss of access to services.

**Notable Changes:**

This version of the agreement adds some clarity around moderation and enforcement on third-party platforms (like Xbox).

**Important Reminders:**

* To understand what data Microsoft collects and how it's used, you should review their Privacy Policy.
* If you have questions about the Terms of Service, you can find more information on Microsoft's website.

Please note that these Terms of Service do not explicitly address concerns outside of the scope of the agreement, such as security or refunds.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

**OpenAI Terms of Use (Consumer)**

These terms describe the relationship between you, the user, and OpenAI, and explain what you can expect when using our products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to our products and services listed on our official terms page.
* **Content and License**: We use your user-submitted content to improve and train our AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (In simpler terms, when you give us your thoughts, ideas, or data, we use it to make our systems smarter, but we follow your choices and the law.)
* **Privacy**: OpenAI follows the guidelines laid out in our published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data we collect and how we use it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If there's a problem, we require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. (This means you can't join a lawsuit with others who have similar issues; instead, you'll go through a private dispute resolution.)
* **Termination**: Either you or OpenAI can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions or concerns, check our published legal contact information at [https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/](https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/).

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waivers means you can't join a group lawsuit, which might reduce the likelihood of significant compensation or changes.
* **No prior explanation available**: Since this is the first version of the Terms of Service, it's not clear how the earlier version differed or how existing users were affected by changes. We recommend keeping an eye on future updates.

Please note that these terms aim to standardize the consumer relationship, but specific provisions may harm or favor you. Always review and ask questions before agreeing to new or changed terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API) governs your relationship with the company for its products and services, including API access, and business solutions like ChatGPT Enterprise and ChatGPT Team.

Here are the key provisions:

### Overview
- This agreement applies to OpenAI services listed on their terms page.
- You can review official announcements about policy updates at community.openai.com.

### Content Submission and Use
- When you use OpenAI services, you may submit content that is used by the company to:
  • Run and improve their AI systems (where you have given consent or permissions).
  • Maybe used to train the AI systems (where applicable, subject to local law).

### Data Handling and Privacy
- Personal data you submit to OpenAI will be handled under their Privacy Policy.
  • You can learn about the types of personal data collected on the OpenAI Privacy Policy page.
  • There's [no further information in the provided TOS about the content of the Privacy Policy](https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/).

### Dispute Resolution
- This version of the TOS contains a [binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) request](https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/topics/dispute-resolution-arbitration), which can be opted out of within 30 days of account opening (for new accounts).
- [Notable exceptions are certain jurisdictions](https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/).

### Termination
- Both parties can terminate this agreement as outlined in the live document (link to the terms is: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/).

### Important Notes:
- Keep an eye out for changes to your relationship with OpenAI and announcements about the company's policies.

For questions or concerns, you're referred to OpenAI's legal page: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

* **Scope (Section 1):** These Terms apply to the products and services described on Anthropic's official terms page. This means that even if you visit or interact with Anthropic through other websites or platforms, these Terms might still apply to you.

This means you'll have 30 days after creating an account to opt out of arbitration. However, Steam (Valve) is an exception to this rule.

**Potential concerns for users:**

* **User Content and License (Section 3):** While Anthropic uses your content to improve their services, the extent of this usage isn't clearly defined. Be aware that your content might be used to train AI/ML systems without explicit user consent.
* **Dispute Resolution (Section 5):** Binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might limit your ability to join or participate in class-action lawsuits, which could prevent you from seeking collective redress for similar grievances.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

**Service Name:** Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (API)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with Anthropic when you use their commercial API products and services. They describe how your data will be used, what happens to any content you submit, and how disputes will be resolved.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These TOS apply to the API products and services listed on Anthropic's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Anthropic uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is processed in accordance with Anthropic's published Privacy Policy. (Note: The actual policy is not linked here, but it's recommended to review it separately.)
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most TOS require binding arbitration, which means you'll have to resolve disputes privately through a third-party process (instead of going to court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, consult Anthropic's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration**: This clause may be unfavorable to users, as it forces them into private dispute resolution instead of allowing access to the court system. (Note: Not all states/jurisdictions will honor arbitration agreements.)
* **Class-Action Waiver**: You may be prevented from joining a class-action lawsuit if disputes arise.

Please note that these Terms of Service may have changed since the last update. Review the document and associated content to ensure you understand the current terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Meta (Facebook) Terms of Service, effective from 2025.

**Summary:** These updated terms govern your relationship with Facebook and outline how you can use their products and services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope and Agreement**: By using Facebook products and services, you agree to these terms. This means you're binding yourself to their rules, whether you sign up or just start using their services.
* **Content and Licensing**: When you upload content, you grant Facebook a license to use it. This allows them to improve and train their AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws. Keep in mind that Facebook might use your content without your explicit consent.
* **Privacy**: The terms refer you to Facebook's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how they process it. It's essential to review this policy to understand what you're agreeing to.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In the event of a dispute, you're required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court). This means you won't be able to file a class-action lawsuit or take your case to court. You have 30 days to opt out of this requirement upon creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either Facebook or you can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions outlined in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Lack of clarity on data usage**: The terms allow Facebook to use your content without explicit consent, which might be a concern for users who value their digital rights.
* **Binding arbitration**: This requirement can limit your access to the traditional court system and class-action lawsuits, which might make it harder to seek redress if you feel wronged by Facebook.

Keep in mind that you can review Facebook's Privacy Policy and TOS document for more information on their policies and practices.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Instagram Terms of Use

The Instagram Terms of Use govern your relationship with Meta, the company that operates Instagram. The terms apply to the products and services described on Meta's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content License:** When you upload content to Instagram, you grant a worldwide non-exclusive license to Meta to use, distribute, and modify it. This means that Meta can use your photos, videos, and posts in various ways, including for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) purposes.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which outlines how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Instagram, you will typically need to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means that you will not be able to join a class-action lawsuit against Instagram.
* **Termination:** Either party (you or Instagram) can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the terms.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can refer to the company's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** The dispute resolution clause requires binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This could make it more difficult for users to seek justice if they are harmed by Instagram's actions.
* **Wide License:** The content license grant may be broad and could allow Meta to use your content in ways that you do not anticipated or agree with.

**Additional Notes:**

* The terms are effective as of 2025 and replace the 2024 version.
* You can find previous versions of the terms at archiv versions.
* You have a 30-day op-out window for new accounts regarding the binding arbitration with class-action waivers, but it is unclear if this applies for renewing accounts.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

**Service Name:** X

The Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with X (Twitter) and its products and services. The key provisions are:

**1. Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on X's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to X, you grant the company a royalty-free, worldwide license to use your content for various purposes, including training machine-learning and generative-AI models. This includes an in-app setting where you can choose to limit how your content is used.
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is subject to X's Privacy Policy, which outlines categories of data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users are required to resolve disputes through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (you can't join a group lawsuit)**. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions listed in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The arbitration and class-action waiver provisions may limit your ability to seek redress and join with others in a lawsuit. (See *Dispute Resolution* above.)

6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Service Name:** TikTok Terms of Service (US)

**Key Provisions:**

* These Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with TikTok and apply to its products and services listed on the official terms page.
* When you share content on TikTok, the company uses it to improve and train its AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable laws.
* Your content can be used for training machine learning (ML) models.
* TikTok's [Privacy Policy](https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/privacy/en) explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* In case of disputes, most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process) with class-action waivers, giving you 30 days to opt out (but note that Steam has removed mandatory arbitration).
* Either party can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.
* For questions, contact TikTok through the provided legal contact information on the TOS page.

**Harmful Clauses to Consider:**

* When using generative-AI (like TikTok's automated content generators), you're responsible for the inputs and outputs. If you remove watermarks or pretend an AI-generated piece is human-made, you may be in breach.
* TikTok can potentially use your content in any way it sees fit (as long as it follows your settings and applicable laws).

**Note:** While the Terms of Service describe how your content is used, it's essential to review TikTok's [Privacy Policy](https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/privacy/en) for more information on data collection and processing.

These Terms of Service seem to prioritize TikTok's interests in maintaining its AI/ML systems, but it's always a good idea to read the full documents and consider seeking advice if you're unsure about the implications.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

The Adobe General Terms of Use govern your relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services you use on the company's terms page.

Here are the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all Adobe products and services.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Adobe, they may use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. However, this is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms cross-reference Adobe's **published Privacy Policy**, which explains what personal data they collect and how they process it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with class-action waivers. This means you can't join a group lawsuit against Adobe. New accounts have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Termination**: Either Adobe or you can end the agreement under certain conditions. (Please note that the document does not specify these conditions.)
* **Contact**: If you have questions, you can look at Adobe's published contact information on their legal page.

As for concerns, please be aware of:

* **Accessing user content**: Adobe now explicitly states they may **access user content via automated and manual methods (which may process the content in some way)** to improve services and software. This is a trade-off for using Adobe's services, but users should be aware of this.
* **Generative-AI models**: Adobe explicitly states they **do not** train generative-AI models on customer cloud content, which is reassuring.
* **Arbitration**: Binding arbitration with class-action waivers is a potential drawback for users, as they lose the right to join group lawsuits.

Keep in mind that Adobe is a prominent company with a strong focus on innovation, and many of their terms align with industry standards. If you have further concerns, I'd be happy to help.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

**Overview of the Zoom Terms of Service**

Zoom is a video conferencing platform, and these Terms of Service (TOS) outline your relationship with Zoom when using their products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service govern your use of Zoom's products and services, described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content on Zoom, such as audio, video, or chat, Zoom can use it to operate, improve, and train their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **License to Service-Generated Data:** Zoom has a broad license to use Service-Generated Data for training AI and ML models, but you can opt-out of this use in your account settings.
* **Privacy:** The Terms of Service cross-reference Zoom's published Privacy Policy, which describes the personal data collected and processing practices.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most provisions require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, but you may opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either you or Zoom can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.

**Clauses to Note:**

* **Section 8 (Content and License):** Zoom uses user-submitted content to train AI and ML systems without explicit customer consent. **User backlash led Zoom to amend this section in August 2023 to allow user opt-outs**.
* **Section 10 (License to Service-Generated Data):** Zoom initially allowed use of Service-Generated Data for training AI and ML models without explicit consent, but **they revised this after user concerns in March 2023**.

**Other Considerations:**

* Remember that some disputes may be resolved through binding arbitration, which can limit your ability to sue in court.
* If you're concerned about specific aspects of Zoom's TOS, review your account settings and check the company's published Privacy Policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ZOOM TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Zoom and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: March 2023 update added broad license over 'Service Generated Data' permitting use to train AI/ML models. Following user backlash in August 2023, Zoom amended Section 10 to explicitly state it does not use audio, video or chat content to train AI models without customer consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Zoom to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230301000000*/https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ .

These Terms of Service govern the relationship between you and LinkedIn, primarily applying to the services and products listed on their official terms page.

Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope of the Agreement**: These terms apply to all products and services provided by LinkedIn, which include the official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you share content on LinkedIn, the company can use it to improve its services and train its AI systems, unless you've set a restriction in your settings or applicable law prohibits it.
* **Privacy**: The company's Privacy Policy outlines the information collected about you, but these terms don't provide explicit details.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court); you can opt out of this within 30 days of creating your account, but doing so may limit your claim options.
* **Termination**: Either you or LinkedIn can terminate the agreement, following conditions listed in the document.

Flagged clauses that may be potentially harmful to the user include:

* **Dispute Resolution**: Requiring binding arbitration may limit users' ability to take their disputes to court, potentially affecting their claim.
* **Content and License**: While users can restrict content usage through settings, default behavior allows LinkedIn to use content for training AI, which users may not be aware of.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Service Name:** GitHub Terms of Service, latest version effective 2026.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms regulate the relationship between you and GitHub, applying to the services described on the company's official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: When you submit content, GitHub uses it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your preferences and applicable law.
3. **Privacy**: GitHub's collected personal data is governed by their published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of data and how it's processed.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, although you can opt out within 30 days of creating a new account.
5. **Termination**: Either you or GitHub can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.

**Concerns:**

* The clause allowing GitHub to use your user-submitted content to train AI features might be concerning to users who do not want their data used in this manner. However, it is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers (mentioned in point 5, "Dispute Resolution") could potentially limit users' rights in a dispute resolution context.
* The fact that Steam is the exception to this provision, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024, makes this a key point for users who want to be aware of their potential options.
* **Note:** The updated terms have not changed significantly from the previous version, as per the company's own description; therefore, there is little information about any changed clause in particular. The main updates described involve additional sharing of personal data with external entities for uses that include AI/ML development, and opt-out preferences being preserved across those entities. 

**Recommendation:** If you have concerns about dispute resolution or the usage of your personal data, review the Privacy Policy and dispute resolution procedures available on GitHub's support website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

Overall, these terms provide a fair overview of your responsibilities as a PayPal user, including how content is used, disputes are resolved, and the agreement can be terminated.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

service_name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions
response:
**Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions**

These terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to its media services like Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms cover many Apple services, including Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content, like photos or music, it can be used by Apple to improve and train its AI and machine-learning systems. You're agreeing to let Apple use this content, but your settings and the law will control how it's used.
* **Data Privacy:** These terms reference Apple's published Privacy Policy, which says how Apple collects and processes your personal data. (Think of your name, email, and location.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** Many disputes must be resolved through private arbitration (a private mediation process instead of going to court) with a class-action waiver. You have 30 days to opt-out of arbitration for new accounts. Be aware that this might limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Termination:** Apple can end the agreement if you break the rules or terminate the service early. You might not get a refund.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can find Apple's contact information on the company website.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** As mentioned earlier, disputes must often go through private arbitration. This might limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit and could be considered unfair by some users.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

These are the Terms of Service for the iCloud service, which is a collection of online services provided by Apple.

**Key Provisions**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all iCloud products and services listed on Apple's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Apple uses user-submitted content to improve and operate its AI and machine learning systems, but only with your settings and applicable law in mind. 
* **Privacy**: The Privacy Policy sets out how Apple collects and processes personal data, but these terms don't provide much detail.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute, you and Apple must use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of a court) with a 30-day opt-out window when you create a new account.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact**: Reach out to Apple's legal team for questions about these terms.

**Harmful Clauses to Users**

* The Terms of Service suggest that Apple can access your stored content for legal or safety reasons. This might raise concerns about how and when Apple will access your data.
* The use of binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of a court) might limit your options for seeking redress.
* The lack of detail in the terms about data collection and processing under the Privacy Policy might make it difficult for users to understand how their personal data is being used.

**Other Points to Note**

* The terms are binding, so it's essential to read and understand what you're agreeing to when using iCloud services.
* You can opt out of binding arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account, but this might not be available if you're part of a group that already has an existing dispute with Apple.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** These are the Pinterest Terms of Service, which outline the rules and responsibilities for using the Pinterest platform.

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms set out the rules for using Pinterest's products and services, including how user-submitted content is used.
* Users should note that their public Pins may be used by Pinterest to train AI/ML models, which is done to provide more tailored recommendations and enhance safety on the platform. 
* Advertisers and merchants are also subject to additional obligations outlined in the Terms.
* The Terms require that users resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of going to court. Class-action lawsuits are waived, except in certain circumstances (e.g. no mandatory arbitration at Steam).
* Either party may terminate the agreement if they want to stop using Pinterest's services.
* For questions or concerns about the Terms, users can contact Pinterest using the provided contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**
* The requirement for binding arbitration (section 5: DISPUTE RESOLUTION) may make it more difficult for users to seek large damages or pursue group lawsuits against Pinterest.
* The use of public Pins to train AI/ML models (section 3:CONTENT AND LICENSE) may be concerning for users who are particular about their online presence or don't want their content used in this way.
* Users should be aware that advertisers and merchants are subject to their own obligations outlined in these Terms, as the document does not provide much detail on this point.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Quora Terms of Service**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Quora, a question-and-answer platform. They apply to all Quora products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and Permissions**: Quora uses your submitted content to improve and operate its AI and machine learning systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Quora's Privacy Policy outlines how it collects and processes your personal data. You can find this policy elsewhere on the Quora website.
* **Termination**: Either Quora or you can terminate the agreement at any time.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with Quora, you agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with some exceptions (currently Steam users can't be forced into arbitration).

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* Quora can use your content to train its AI and machine learning systems without your explicit consent.
* You agree to binding arbitration, which may limit your rights to seek compensation in court. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Other Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service require you to follow specific rules for Quora's AI chatbot platform, Poe. Quora can use user prompts and responses to improve Poe and its partner models.
* These Terms of Service may be updated from time to time, so be sure to check the Quora website for the latest version.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Summary:** These terms of service govern your relationship with 23andMe and its products and services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all 23andMe products and services, as listed on its official terms page.
* **Content and License**: You grant 23andMe a license to use your user-submitted content, such as DNA data, to operate and improve its services. This includes training its AI/ML systems (more on this later).
* **Privacy**: 23andMe's published Privacy Policy sets out what data is collected and how it's processed. However, the exact details are not provided in these terms.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through **mandatory binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers**. 5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name:** Twitch Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

These terms govern your relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services offered on Twitch's official terms page.

* **Content and License:** When you submit content, such as videos or streams, Twitch can use it to improve and train their AI/ML systems, but only if your settings allow it.
* **Privacy:** Twitch's Privacy Policy sets out what personal data they collect and how it's processed. (Note: This document links to a separate policy, but you should review both to understand how your data is used.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means you cannot sue Twitch in a court. Additionally, there are class-action waivers, which means you cannot join a group lawsuit against Twitch.
* **Termination:** Either Twitch or you can terminate the agreement, but the document does not specify the conditions.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waivers can make it difficult for users to seek redress if they have a dispute with Twitch. This means you may not be able to hold Twitch accountable in a court of law.
* **Termination:** The lack of specific conditions for termination may leave users unsure of what they need to do to avoid account closure.
* **Data Use:** The ability for Twitch to use your content for AI/ML training, even if you don't opt-in, might be concerning to users who value data privacy.

Keep in mind that these are general observations based on the provided Terms of Service, and it's essential to review the full document and Twitch's Privacy Policy to understand your specific rights and responsibilities.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

The service is called the "Roblox Terms of Use".

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**What's covered**: These terms apply to your relationship with Roblox and govern your use of the company's products and services.

**Default settings and user protection**: 
* Accounts under 13 years old are default-private, meaning only they can see their content.
* You may be required to provide consent from a parent or guardian to use certain features.

**Content and data usage**:
* Roblox can use your submitted content, but only as permitted by your settings and applicable laws.
* Content might be used to improve or train Roblox's artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems.

**Data protection**:
* For more information on data collection and processing, see the company's published Privacy Policy.
* This policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's used.

**Dispute resolution**:
* Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, which is a private process instead of a court trial. 
* There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, after which you won't be able to opt out.
* Note that not all countries may offer arbitration, and class-action waivers apply.

**Termination**:
* You or Roblox can terminate the agreement under certain conditions outlined in the live document.

**Contact**:
* If you have questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information on the Roblox website.

As for potential harm, be aware that the following clause may impact you:

* Mandatory binding arbitration with class-action waivers can limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits and might make it harder to hold Roblox accountable for certain issues.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .
